The proposition semantics say blocker_moved is true when the cell in front of the door holds no ball, not when no ball exists anywhere. Also, the candidate references undefined variables `dx` and `dy` inside the generator expression (`for dx, dy in [(x, y)]` is present but the door position is never computed, so the front-of-door cell is not identified). CHANGES REQUIRED: The `blocker_moved` predicate is wrong. It scans every door in the grid and returns true whenever any door's left neighbor is not a ball — this is not the documented semantics. The documented truth condition is simply that the fixed cell in front of the door, `(dx - 1, dy)`, holds no ball, where `(dx, dy)` is the door's own cell (the ball starts at `(dx - 1, dy)`). The candidate instead checks `x - 1` for every door cell, which (a) invents a relative offset from an arbitrary door location instead of checking the specific cell in front of the door, and (b) can return true for reasons unrelated to the ball, e.g. when the door's left neighbor is empty or a wall even before the ball has been moved — so it can fire before `blocker_moved` is actually true, breaking the constraint ordering in the RM. The necessary fix, in plain language: find the door (there is exactly one), take the cell at `(door_x - 1, door_y)`, and return true if and only if that cell is empty or does not contain a ball; a ball held in the agent's hand is not on the grid and therefore counts as moved. Keep `has_door_key` as written — it is correct.
